h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Farragut, TN
hero_subtitle: Farragut homeowners can compare free quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers, whether the house is off Campbell Station Road or down near Fort Loudoun Lake. No obligation to hire.
intro: Farragut is a separate town, not a Knoxville neighborhood. Residents voted to incorporate in January 1980, partly to head off annexation by Knoxville, and the population grew from 17,720 in 2000 to 23,506 in 2020. The town sits in hilly country between Blackoak Ridge and Fort Loudoun Lake, with Kingston Pike through the middle and most of the town south of I-40/I-75. The area was first known as Campbell's Station, and the town's name honors Admiral David Farragut, who was born nearby.

sections.heading: Subdivisions from the 1970s to today
body: Much of Farragut was built during the westward suburban growth that followed the completion of I-40 in the 1960s. Fox Den, centered on its country club and 18-hole golf course, has mostly 1970s and 1980s homes, and Village Green off Old Colony Parkway was already settled by the mid-1980s. On the town's eastern edge, Concord Hills lies south of Kingston Pike and Thornton Heights sits to the north near Lovell Road.

On a house built in the 1970s or 1980s, ask each roofer to confirm how many shingle layers are on the deck and to probe the decking for soft spots. Tear-off, decking replacement and new flashing should appear as separate line items, which makes the quotes much easier to compare.

sections.heading: Slopes, trees and summer storms
body: Farragut's rolling terrain puts many houses on sloped, wooded lots. Shade slows drying after rain, leaves load up gutters and valleys, and big limbs over a roof become a puncture risk when a thunderstorm comes through.

During a severe storm on July 14, 2016, Farragut High School lost the roof of a softball dugout and shingles from its weight room, and trees came down on nearby streets. After any strong storm, look for missing shingles, creased tabs and granules collecting at the downspouts, and get an inspection before a small problem turns into a ceiling stain.

sections.heading: Town rules, HOAs and licensing
body: Because Farragut is incorporated, building questions go to the Town's own Planning & Codes office. Ask each roofer whether your job needs a permit and who will apply for it.

If your subdivision has a homeowners association or recorded covenants, read them before choosing a shingle color or switching to metal, since architectural review may be required. Share any approved-product list with the roofers you are matched with so every quote uses a compliant material and you are not waiting on approval after the old roof is already off.

sections.heading: Before the roofers visit
body: Gather whatever paperwork exists on the current roof: the year it went on, the shingle brand and color, and any transferable warranty from a previous owner. On the day of the visit, clear a path to the attic hatch. A look at the underside of the deck shows old leaks, ventilation problems and past patch jobs that cannot be seen from the driveway, and it helps every roofer quote the same job.

roofing_notes: On 1970s and 1980s homes, confirm the number of existing shingle layers and check the decking before comparing prices.
Wooded, sloped lots mean gutter cleaning, gutter guards and limb trimming belong in the conversation.
Read HOA covenants before changing shingle color or material; some require architectural approval.
Farragut has its own Planning & Codes office, so confirm who pulls any permit.

faqs.q: Is Farragut part of Knoxville?
faqs.a: No. Farragut has been its own town since residents voted to incorporate in January 1980, and it has a mayor, aldermen and a Planning & Codes office of its own. It is mostly in Knox County, with a small part in Loudon County. Many addresses use ZIP code 37934 and some use 37922, so your mailing address alone may not tell you whether you are inside town limits.

faqs.q: What license should a roofer have for a Farragut job?
faqs.a: Most of Farragut is in Knox County, which adopted Tennessee's Home Improvement law. A residential roofing contract from $3,000 to $24,999 there requires a state Home Improvement license, and a job of $25,000 or more requires a state contractor's license. Ask for the license number and proof of insurance, and look the number up with the Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance.

faqs.q: Do I need HOA approval before reroofing in Farragut?
faqs.a: It depends on your subdivision. Some neighborhoods have covenants or an architectural review committee that must sign off on new colors or materials, and others say nothing about roofs. Check your documents or ask the HOA board before you sign a contract, and tell your roofer about any approval timeline so it is built into the schedule.

name: West Knoxville
title: West Knoxville Roofing Quotes | Compare Local Roofers
meta_description: Get free roofing quotes in West Knoxville, from West Hills and Cedar Bluff to Rocky Hill. Up to 3 local roofers, each licensed and insured. No obligation.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in West Knoxville
hero_subtitle: Ranch houses in West Hills, townhomes in Rocky Hill, newer two-stories near Pellissippi Parkway: tell us about your West Knoxville roof and compare up to 3 free quotes from licensed, insured roofers.
intro: West Knoxville is the part of the city that spreads west from Sequoyah Hills along Kingston Pike to the Farragut town line. It filled in over several decades: West Hills opened in the 1950s, West Town Mall was completed in 1972, and the Turkey Creek retail complex opened in 2002. That layering means one street can hold a 70-year-old ranch house and the next a much newer two-story, and the roofers you hire here should be comfortable with both.

sections.heading: West Hills and the 1950s ranch house
body: West Hills was Knoxville's first major post-World War II subdivision and the first made up mostly of modern ranch-style houses. Developer Morgan Schubert assembled it from four family farms, and Knoxville's 1954 Parade of Homes showcased new houses on Stockton Drive. The neighborhood has kept its residential character, helped by an active community association.

Ranch roofs are long and fairly low, so water moves off them more slowly than off a steep roof. When one of these houses is reroofed, pay close attention to flashing at chimneys, valleys and roof-to-wall joints. If an earlier owner added a carport or enclosed porch under a nearly flat section, ask whether that part needs a low-slope membrane instead of shingles.

sections.heading: Cedar Bluff, Rocky Hill and the Northshore side
body: North of I-40, Cedar Bluff sits at the heart of one of Knoxville's major commercial corridors, with office and technology parks mixed in among residential streets off Cedar Bluff Road, Park West Boulevard and Middlebrook Pike. South of Kingston Pike, Rocky Hill lies north and west of Northshore Drive, east of Wallace Road and south of Westland Drive, with both single-family houses and townhomes.

With a townhome or condo, the roof may belong to the association rather than to you, so check your documents before you request quotes. If you manage an office or retail building along the corridor, pick the commercial roof option when you fill out the form.

sections.heading: Wind, trees and storm damage
body: In August 2023 an EF-2 tornado cut through the Devanshire subdivision near Pellissippi Parkway and Lovell Road, peeling roofs and shingles off houses and splitting the trusses on at least one home. A tornado like that is rare, but an ordinary thunderstorm can do similar damage on a smaller scale when a large tree comes down on a house.
After a storm, photograph the damage from the ground, cover any opening with a tarp if it is safe to do so, and talk to your insurer before you sign anything.

sections.heading: Fixing what the original builders skipped
body: On a mid-century house, a new roof is a chance to correct things the original builders never planned for: undersized gutters, little or no ridge ventilation, and bathroom fans that vent into the attic instead of outdoors. Ask each roofer whether the quote adds ridge and soffit ventilation, and whether they will run bath fan ducts out through the roof while the deck is exposed. Those items are easy to add while the roof is open and much harder to add later.

roofing_notes: 1950s and 1960s ranch roofs have low pitch, so flashing and any near-flat additions need extra attention.
Townhome and condo owners should confirm whether the association owns the roof.
Mature trees on older streets make limb clearance and gutter cleaning part of roof upkeep.
Confirm whether your address is inside Knoxville city limits, since that decides which codes office handles any permit.

faqs.q: Is West Knoxville a separate city?
faqs.a: No. West Knoxville is a section of the City of Knoxville, not its own municipality. It was annexed in stages, with Sequoyah Hills and Lyons View Pike coming in 1917 and Bearden and West Hills in 1962. Farragut, farther west, is a separate town, and some homes with a Knoxville mailing address are in unincorporated Knox County, so check before assuming which local rules apply.

faqs.q: Can a low-pitched West Hills ranch roof take architectural shingles?
faqs.a: Usually, as long as each roof plane meets the shingle manufacturer's minimum slope. Very low sections, such as an enclosed porch or carport roof, may need a membrane instead. Ask each roofer to measure the pitch of every plane and to note in the quote which material goes where, so you are comparing the same scope of work.

faqs.q: What should I do in the first day after storm damage?
faqs.a: Make sure no one is in rooms with a sagging or wet ceiling, and stay away from any downed lines. Take dated photos, move valuables away from leaks, and get the opening covered. Then call your insurer and request quotes. The roofers you are matched with usually reach out within 24 to 48 hours, and you are never obligated to hire any of them.

name: Bearden
title: Bearden Roofing Quotes | Knoxville, TN Local Roofers
meta_description: Free roofing quotes for Bearden homes, from Forest Heights to the Kingston Pike corridor. Compare up to 3 licensed, insured Knoxville roofers, no obligation.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Bearden, Knoxville
hero_subtitle: Older houses, big trees and historic streets. Bearden homeowners can request free, no-obligation quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers serving Forest Heights, Sequoyah Hills and Kingston Pike.
intro: Bearden is one of Knoxville's older suburbs, strung along Kingston Pike between Lyons View Pike and Sutherland Avenue. It began as a settlement called Erin near Fourth Creek, took the Bearden name in the late 1800s when a post office opened, and grew up around the Southern Railway and the old Dixie-Lee Highway before the city annexed it in 1962. Today it blends pre-war houses, post-war homes and a busy commercial strip under a heavy canopy of mature trees.

sections.heading: Forest Heights and the pre-war houses
body: Forest Heights, just north of Sutherland Avenue, was first built up in the 1920s and 1930s. Its oldest section, along Forest Hills Boulevard, is a National Register historic district built between 1928 and 1938, with Tudor Revival, Colonial Revival, Dutch Colonial Revival and French Eclectic houses. Most of the neighborhood's other homes went up after World War II, and Knoxville annexed it in 1960.

Steep gables, dormers and multiple valleys are typical of those revival styles, and each one adds flashing work and labor to a reroof. If your house still has slate, clay tile or another original material, ask whether the roofer repairs it or only replaces it, since not every crew works with those materials.

sections.heading: Kingston Pike's historic stretch
body: Along Kingston Pike, addresses running roughly from 2728 to 3643 make up the Kingston Pike Historic District, added to the National Register in 1996, with buildings dating from 1834 to 1930. A National Register listing on its own does not limit what a private owner does with a roof.

A few individual properties along the Pike also carry a local H-1 historic overlay, which is a separate, city-level designation. If you are unsure which applies to your property, check with Knoxville-Knox County Planning before changing roofing materials.

sections.heading: Shade, gutters and the commercial strip
body: Bearden's shade is part of its appeal, but it keeps roofs damp and fills gutters fast in the fall. Moss and dark algae streaks tend to show up first on shaded, north-facing slopes, and limbs hanging over the roof can puncture it in a summer storm.

Bearden also has more than 30 shopping centers and several dozen office buildings. Flat and low-slope commercial roofs are a separate specialty from houses, and the quote form has its own commercial choice for them.

sections.heading: Sequoyah Hills next door
body: East of Bearden, Sequoyah Hills was one of Knoxville's first suburbs, developed from the mid-1920s on a peninsula in a bend of the Tennessee River, with Cherokee Boulevard looping around its edge. Robert Foust's Talahi subdivision required English Cottage or Colonial Revival houses, and later builders added Tudor Revival, Georgian Revival, Minimal Traditional and even art moderne homes. With that much variety, the right material and approach can differ from one house to the next on the same street.

roofing_notes: Revival-style houses from the 1920s and 1930s have steep gables, dormers and valleys that add flashing work.
Ask whether a roofer repairs slate, tile or other original materials before assuming full replacement.
Shaded north slopes collect moss and algae; plan for regular gutter cleaning and limb trimming.
A few Kingston Pike properties have a local H-1 overlay, so check before changing materials.

faqs.q: Is Bearden inside Knoxville city limits?
faqs.a: Yes. Bearden was a separate community until the City of Knoxville annexed it in 1962, and neighboring Forest Heights was annexed in 1960. City rules therefore apply to most Bearden addresses. The main ZIP code is 37919, and some nearby homes, including parts of West Hills, use 37909.

faqs.q: Does National Register status limit what I can do with my roof?
faqs.a: Not by itself. Being inside a National Register district, such as the Kingston Pike Historic District or the Forest Hills Boulevard district, recognizes a property's history but does not restrict privately funded work. A local H-1 historic overlay is different and can involve design review. If you are not sure which applies, ask Knoxville-Knox County Planning before you change materials.

faqs.q: A limb came through my roof. What comes first?
faqs.a: Get everyone out of the affected rooms and keep clear of wet ceilings and any downed power lines. Once it is safe, take photos, have a tree service remove the limb, and get the opening tarped. After that, contact your insurance company and send in a quote request; matched roofers typically call or email within 24 to 48 hours.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Powell, TN
hero_subtitle: From the old Powell Station area to homes along Emory Road and Brickyard Road, request a free roof quote in Powell and hear from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers. No obligation.
intro: Powell is an unincorporated community in north Knox County, not a city, and it was once called Powell Station after the train stop named for local resident Columbus Powell. It lies in the Beaver Creek valley between Copper Ridge and Beaver Ridge, roughly between I-75 on the east and Clinton Highway on the west, with Emory Road as its main east-west route. The 2020 census counted 13,802 residents and 5,766 housing units in the Powell census-designated place.

sections.heading: From brickyards to suburbs
body: In the early 1900s the railroad drove Powell's economy, and local brickmakers used mud from Beaver Creek, shipping their bricks out by rail. The old station still stands in what residents call downtown Powell. On Clinton Highway, the Airplane Service Station, built in 1930 in the shape of a plane, has been on the National Register since 2004.

Housing today ranges from older homes near the original town to newer subdivisions, so roof ages can vary a lot from one street to the next. If you just bought a house, ask the roofer to judge the age and condition of the existing roof on site rather than relying on the listing.

sections.heading: Ridge slopes and the valley floor
body: Because Powell sits between two long, narrow ridges, some homes are on low ground near Beaver Creek and others are up on the slopes. Ridge-side houses take more wind, so ask about the manufacturer's high-wind nailing pattern and sealed starter strips along the eaves and rakes.

Lower lots collect runoff from the hills above them. On those properties, gutters and downspouts that carry water well away from the foundation matter as much as the shingles, and a quote that includes new drip edge and properly sized downspouts is worth a close look.

sections.heading: Questions worth asking a Powell roofer
body: Ask how the crew will protect landscaping and driveways, especially on sloped lots where placing a dumpster or a material delivery is tricky. Ask whether the quote includes new pipe boots, step flashing and ridge vents, not just shingles.

Get the warranty terms in writing as well. The shingle manufacturer's coverage on materials is separate from the roofer's own workmanship warranty, and you want to know who to call, and for how long, if a problem shows up after the job.

sections.heading: The Emory Road corridor
body: Emory Road, State Route 131, is Powell's main street. In 2013 county planners approved a shopping complex on the site of a former airstrip next to the I-75 interchange at Emory Road, and business owners along the corridor can request quotes for a store or office roof as well as a house.

Before you request quotes, take a few photos of the roof from each side of the house and note any ceiling stains or attic drips. Sharing those with the roofers you are matched with speeds up the first conversation.

roofing_notes: Ridge-slope homes see more wind; ask about high-wind nailing and sealed starter strips.
Valley-floor lots near Beaver Creek need gutters and downspouts that move water away from the house.
Roof ages vary widely between older homes and newer subdivisions, so have the existing roof assessed in person.
Knox County requires a state Home Improvement license for residential jobs from $3,000 to $24,999.

faqs.q: Is Powell part of Knoxville?
faqs.a: No. Powell is an unincorporated census-designated place in Knox County, even though homes there have their own Powell mailing address and ZIP code, 37849. There is no city government, so Knox County handles local building questions. When you submit the form, your Powell ZIP code helps match you with roofers who work in north Knox County.

faqs.q: What license should a Powell roofer have?
faqs.a: For a house in Knox County, a roofing contract between $3,000 and $24,999 requires a Tennessee Home Improvement license, because the county adopted that state law. Above that range, the roofer needs a full state contractor's license instead. Ask for the license number and a certificate of liability insurance, and check the number with the Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance.

faqs.q: My house is on a ridge. Do I need a different kind of roof?
faqs.a: Not necessarily a different product, but installation details matter more on an exposed lot. Ask whether the roofer will follow the manufacturer's high-wind nailing pattern, use sealed starter strips at the eaves and rakes, and ventilate the attic properly. Some shingle warranties cover higher wind speeds only when those steps are followed, so ask for the wind rating in the quote.

name: Halls
title: Halls Crossroads Roofing Quotes | Halls, TN Roofers
meta_description: Free roofing quotes for Halls Crossroads homes in north Knox County. Compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers for repairs or a new roof, with no obligation.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Halls Crossroads, TN
hero_subtitle: Whether you live in Grove Point or off Maynardville Pike, one short form puts your Halls Crossroads roof in front of up to 3 licensed, insured roofers. Free for homeowners, with no obligation.
intro: Halls, or Halls Crossroads, takes its name from the Thomas Hall family, who settled on the north side of Black Oak Ridge around 1796, and from the store that stood where Emory Road crosses Maynardville Pike. It has no municipal government of its own; the Census Bureau counts it as a census-designated place, with 10,341 residents in 2020. Black Oak Ridge and Beaver Ridge separate it from Fountain City to the south, and Beaver Creek runs through the middle of the community.

sections.heading: Neighborhoods and housing
body: Halls grew from a rural crossroads into a suburb, and its housing reflects both. Subdivisions such as Grove Point, Brier Meadows and the neighborhoods off Cedar Crossing Road sit alongside older homes on the main roads, and the Halls Stockyards cattle auction is a reminder of the community's farming roots.

If you own a townhome with an association fee, read the documents to see whether the roof is your responsibility or the association's before you collect quotes. For a detached house, the age of the current roof matters more than the age of the house, so find any receipts or permit records before you call.

sections.heading: Beaver Creek, ridges and runoff
body: Beaver Creek drains the heart of Halls, and the Halls Greenway follows its banks. Homes on the lower ground near the creek benefit most from gutters sized for heavy downpours, downspout extensions and splash blocks that keep roof runoff away from crawlspaces.

On the ridge slopes, exposure is the bigger issue. Wind lifts shingle edges, and tall trees on the ridges can drop limbs onto roofs below. Having a roofer look things over after a strong storm is a lot cheaper than discovering a slow leak months later in soaked attic insulation.

sections.heading: Plenty of rain to shed
body: Knoxville's 1991-2020 normals from the National Weather Service in Morristown show close to 52 inches of precipitation and 4.6 inches of snow a year, and Halls gets the same regional weather. Most of that water arrives as rain, so a roof here has to shed a lot of it.

That makes flashing around chimneys and walls, valley details and gutter capacity worth as much attention as the shingle brand. When you compare quotes, check that each one says how valleys will be lined and whether ice and water barrier goes in the valleys and around penetrations.

sections.heading: Buying, selling and the crossroads
body: If you are buying a house in Halls, a roofer's inspection before closing is worth arranging. Ask for photos and a written estimate, because a home inspector's note that a roof is near the end of its life is a starting point, not a price.

The commercial core around the crossroads includes older shopping-center buildings, some of them empty, and redevelopment ideas since the 2010s have included a mixed-use town center and a greenway system.

roofing_notes: Lots near Beaver Creek need gutters and downspout extensions that carry runoff away from crawlspaces.
Ridge-slope homes are more exposed to wind; check shingle edges after strong storms.
Townhome owners should confirm whether the association or the owner is responsible for the roof.
With close to 52 inches of precipitation a year, valley and chimney flashing deserve as much attention as the shingle choice.

faqs.q: Is this the same Halls as the town in West Tennessee?
faqs.a: No. This page covers Halls Crossroads, the unincorporated community in north Knox County that uses ZIP codes 37938 and 37918. There is also a town named Halls in Lauderdale County, in West Tennessee near the Mississippi River. This service connects homeowners with roofers in the Knoxville area, so it is meant for the Knox County community.

faqs.q: Who handles building rules in Halls?
faqs.a: Halls Crossroads is not incorporated, so it has no city codes department and Knox County government covers it. Your roofer should know whether the job needs a county permit, so confirm which of you is responsible for getting it. Knox County also requires roofers to hold a state Home Improvement license for residential work between $3,000 and $24,999, so ask for that number too.

faqs.q: Should I replace gutters at the same time as the roof?
faqs.a: It often makes sense if the gutters are undersized, sagging or pulling away from the fascia, because new drip edge and gutters can go on together. In low spots near Beaver Creek, ask about larger downspouts and extensions. Have the gutter work listed as its own line in each quote so you can compare it fairly.

name: Maryville
title: Maryville, TN Roofing Quotes | Blount County Roofers
meta_description: Get free roofing quotes in Maryville, TN, from College Hill to Montvale Road. Compare up to 3 licensed, insured Blount County roofers with no obligation.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Maryville, TN
hero_subtitle: Victorian on Indiana Avenue or newer house toward the foothills, Maryville homeowners can line up free quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured Blount County roofers, with no obligation.
intro: Maryville is the county seat of Blount County, incorporated in 1795 and named for Mary Grainger Blount, wife of territorial governor William Blount. It sits in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains, with Chilhowee Mountain rising to the south and its twin city, Alcoa, along its northern edge. Maryville College, founded in 1819, anchors the older part of town, and the city had 31,907 residents at the 2020 census.

sections.heading: Historic homes near downtown and the college
body: South of downtown, the Indiana Avenue Historic District was added to the National Register in 1989. Its nomination counts ninety houses, eighty of them built between about 1880 and 1939, in Late Victorian, Colonial Revival and Craftsman bungalow styles, on about 33 acres roughly bounded by Goddard Street, Court Street, Indiana Avenue and Cates Street. The surrounding College Hill area is a local historic district, and Maryville College has its own National Register listing.

Roofs on houses like these are rarely simple: Victorian homes have hips, gables and dormers, and bungalows have deep overhangs with exposed rafter tails. Ask whether the quote covers repairing fascia, soffits and rafter ends where an old roof leaked, and whether the roofer has worked on homes in a historic district.

sections.heading: Foothills weather
body: Maryville's July averages run from about 69 to 87 degrees and January's from about 29 to 46. That brings repeated freeze-thaw cycles in winter and long, hot afternoons on dark shingles in summer, which is hard on sealant strips and on attics without enough ventilation.

Homes on open hillsides toward the mountain are more exposed to wind than sheltered lots in town. Ask each roofer about intake and exhaust ventilation and the shingle's wind rating, and make sure both are written into the quote.

Summer heat tests the attic as much as the shingles. A roof deck that runs hot ages shingles faster and raises cooling bills, so ask whether the roofer will balance soffit intake against ridge exhaust instead of simply adding more vents.

sections.heading: Neighborhoods and corridors
body: Outside the historic core, Maryville spreads along Broadway, Lamar Alexander Parkway (US 321), Montvale Road and William Blount Drive. Broadway, the main street downtown, carries parts of US 411 and US 129. Some subdivisions, including The Park at Royal Oaks, have homeowners associations, so check whether a change in shingle color or material needs approval.

Downtown's look owes a lot to the 1970s Now Town renewal project, which created Bicentennial Greenbelt Park, and many retailers later moved out to Foothills Mall at the junction of US 129 and US 411. Older brick commercial buildings near downtown often have flat or low-slope roofs with internal drains or scuppers. Those call for a roofer who works with commercial membranes, so select the commercial project type when you request quotes.

roofing_notes: Victorian and Craftsman homes in the College Hill area often need fascia, soffit or rafter-tail repairs along with the roof.
Ask about attic ventilation; summer heat and winter freeze-thaw cycles are hard on shingles.
Check HOA rules in subdivisions such as The Park at Royal Oaks before changing roof color or material.
Blount County is outside the state Home Improvement license program, so vet insurance and references closely on jobs under $25,000.

faqs.q: Does a Maryville roofer need a state license?
faqs.a: For jobs of $25,000 or more, yes, because Tennessee requires a contractor's license in every county. Blount County is not one of the nine counties that adopted the state Home Improvement law, so smaller residential jobs there do not need that separate license. On any job, ask for proof of liability insurance, workers' compensation coverage if the roofer has employees, and a written contract.

faqs.q: What should a roofing contract tied to an insurance claim include?
faqs.a: Tennessee requires a roofer on an insurance-paid job to give you, before you sign, a business address and phone number, any license numbers, a detailed description of the damage and repairs, and a written notice of your right to cancel. That right lets you back out before midnight on the third business day after your insurer says all or part of the claim is not covered.

faqs.q: Is Alcoa part of Maryville?
faqs.a: No. Alcoa is a separate city that borders Maryville to the north, and the two are often called twin cities. Both are in Blount County, and you can request quotes for an address in either one through this page. Maryville addresses use ZIP codes 37801, 37803 and 37804.

name: Oak Ridge
title: Oak Ridge, TN Roofing Quotes | Compare Local Roofers
meta_description: Oak Ridge, TN roofing quotes for cemesto houses, flat-tops and newer homes alike. Requesting is free, and as many as 3 licensed, insured roofers respond.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Oak Ridge, TN
hero_subtitle: Cemesto, flat-top or new build, your Oak Ridge roof can get free quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers, from the original wartime townsite to Rarity Ridge. Nothing to sign.
intro: Oak Ridge was built from scratch in 1942 as a Manhattan Project production site, which is where the nicknames Secret City and Atomic City come from. Houses went up quickly, many of them made with cemesto panels of bonded cement and asbestos, and a lot of those wartime homes are still lived in. The city was incorporated in 1959 and lies in both Anderson and Roane counties, with Melton Hill Lake on its east side and Watts Bar Lake to the south.

sections.heading: Alphabet houses and the original townsite
body: The wartime houses came in standard designs labeled with letters, which is why they are known as alphabet houses. The National Park Service lists cemesto types A through H and flat-top designs in types A, B, C, S and V. The Oak Ridge Historic District, added to the National Register in 1991, covers much of the original townsite, roughly bounded by East Drive, Outer and West Outer drives, Louisiana Avenue and Tennessee Avenue.

Before a tear-off on one of these houses, ask the roofer how they would handle cemesto panels or other original materials that might contain asbestos. Disturbing those materials can call for testing and special handling, so it is better to settle that before work starts.

sections.heading: Flat-tops need a different roof
body: The flat-top designs are not shingle roofs. Asphalt shingles are not made for nearly flat surfaces, so these houses typically use a membrane such as modified bitumen, TPO or EPDM.

If you own a flat-top, ask each roofer which system they recommend, how they will handle drainage at the edges, and whether they can add insulation above the deck while the roof is open. Ponding water is the usual enemy on a low-slope roof, so a good quote explains where the water goes.

sections.heading: Later neighborhoods, ridges and lakes
body: Beyond the townsite, the city kept filling in: Woodland, with its curving, alphabetically named streets, Emory Valley, Hendrix Creek and Gamble Valley, and more recently the master-planned Rarity Ridge community at The Preserve at Oak Ridge, which has recorded covenants.

Oak Ridge is laid out among long ridges, including Black Oak Ridge, East Fork Ridge and Pine Ridge, so many lots are wooded and sloped. Homes near Melton Hill Lake or Watts Bar Lake can also catch wind off the water. Ask about drip edge, gutter guards for leaf-heavy lots and the shingle's wind rating.

sections.heading: Duplexes and shared roofs
body: In the Woodland area, the historic houses are mostly single-family models, while neighboring Scarboro is dominated by duplexes. On a duplex, one roof usually covers two households, so talk with the owner next door before you reroof. Replacing only your half can leave a visible color line and a weak seam at the party wall, and doing both halves as one job avoids that.

roofing_notes: Ask how a roofer handles possibly asbestos-containing cemesto or other original materials before tear-off.
Flat-top houses need a low-slope membrane system, not shingles.
Rarity Ridge and other planned communities have recorded covenants worth reading before you pick a new color.
Wooded ridge lots and lakeside homes call for gutter guards and a written wind rating.

faqs.q: Is my Oak Ridge home in Anderson County or Roane County?
faqs.a: It could be either. Most of Oak Ridge is in Anderson County, but part of the city lies in Roane County, and addresses on both sides use ZIP code 37830. Your property tax bill or the county assessor's website will tell you which county you are in. That can matter for permits and taxes, but you can request roofing quotes from either side here.

faqs.q: Can an original cemesto house get a modern roof?
faqs.a: Yes. The main questions are what is under the current roofing and whether any original materials contain asbestos. Ask the roofer whether they will have suspect materials tested before tearing off, how they would handle a positive result, and whether that cost is in the quote or listed separately. Settling this early avoids a stalled job.

faqs.q: Are there neighborhood rules to check before reroofing?
faqs.a: If you live in a planned community such as Rarity Ridge, read the recorded covenants and any architectural review requirements before you pick a new color or material. Older neighborhoods may not have an association at all, but it is still worth a quick check of your deed and any neighborhood covenants before you sign a contract.

name: Clinton
title: Clinton, TN Roofing Quotes | Anderson County Roofers
meta_description: Get free roofing quotes in Clinton, TN, the Anderson County seat, for homes or downtown buildings. Compare up to three bids from insured, licensed roofers.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Clinton, TN
hero_subtitle: Own a home on the ridges or a storefront on Main or Market Street? Clinton property owners can request free quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers, with no obligation to hire.
intro: Clinton is the county seat of Anderson County, founded in 1801 as Burrville and renamed in 1809. The city sits on the Clinch River, along a stretch that is technically part of Melton Hill Lake, and it is ringed by long, narrow ridges. Downtown centers on Main and Market streets, while US 25W and State Route 61 lead out toward Knoxville, Norris and Interstate 75. The 2020 census counted 10,056 residents.

sections.heading: Downtown's historic buildings
body: Clinton became an accredited Tennessee Main Street community in 2021, and its historic downtown runs along Main and Market streets. The oldest remaining building in the district, at 320 N. Main St., dates to the 1890s, and five downtown buildings that shared a state improvement grant in 2022 were built between 1890 and 1940. Market Street reopened in July 2026 after a $9.9 million rebuild of its utilities, sidewalks and lighting.

Many storefronts of that era have low-slope roofs behind parapet walls, and the flashing, wall caps and drains along those parapets need careful inspection. Downtown building owners should mark their request as commercial so the roofers know what they are bidding on.

sections.heading: Homes on the ridges
body: Clinton's residential streets climb the ridges around downtown and spread out along Charles G. Seivers Boulevard, Dutch Valley Road and the South Clinton area. On wooded lots, leaves pile up in gutters and valleys, and limbs over the roof need trimming before they become storm damage.
On a house built into a hillside, ask how the roofer will stage materials and the dumpster, and whether protecting the driveway and lawn is included in the price.

sections.heading: What to check before you hire
body: Anderson County never opted into Tennessee's Home Improvement licensing program, so for jobs under $25,000, insurance, references and a clear contract are your main protections. For larger jobs, ask for the roofer's Tennessee contractor's license number.

Get the scope in writing: tear-off, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, cleanup and a per-sheet price for any decking that has to be replaced, along with the warranty terms. That way an unexpected rotten board does not turn into an argument halfway through the job.

sections.heading: Along the Clinch River
body: South of downtown, the city's 370-acre Aspire park opened in October 2024, and the former Magnet Mills site beside the river is a 7-acre redevelopment property. The Clinch was once known for its freshwater pearls, a trade that faded after Melton Hill Dam changed the river.

If your house sits on low ground near the river or a creek, keep gutters clear and downspouts discharging well away from the foundation, and ask the roofer to confirm the attic is venting moist air out instead of trapping it.

roofing_notes: Downtown storefronts built between 1890 and 1940 often have low-slope roofs behind parapets; inspect flashing and wall caps.
Hillside lots need a plan for staging materials and protecting driveways and lawns.
No Home Improvement license is required in Anderson County, so insurance and references are the main checks on smaller jobs.
Ask for a per-sheet decking replacement price so surprises are priced up front.

faqs.q: Is Lake City the same place as Rocky Top?
faqs.a: Yes. The Anderson County town north of Clinton began as Coal Creek, became Lake City in 1936 after Norris Dam created Norris Lake, and was renamed Rocky Top in 2014. Some older records, and the post office for ZIP code 37769, may still say Lake City. Homeowners there can request roofing quotes through this page.

faqs.q: I own a building downtown. Can I get commercial roofing quotes?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose the commercial option on the form and describe the building, including whether the roof sits behind a parapet and roughly how large it is. Older buildings on Main and Market streets can have several roof layers from past repairs, so ask each roofer to check what is underneath before quoting a full replacement.

faqs.q: How should I compare quotes from Clinton roofers?
faqs.a: Line the quotes up by scope, not just the total. Check that each covers tear-off, underlayment, ice and water barrier in the valleys, flashing, ventilation, decking replacement pricing and cleanup. On hillside homes, access and decking condition can change the final price, so make sure those lines are spelled out the same way in every quote.

name: Lenoir City
title: Lenoir City, TN Roofing Quotes | Loudon County Roofers
meta_description: Free roofing quotes for Lenoir City homes, from downtown to lake lots on Fort Loudoun Lake. Get up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers at no cost.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Lenoir City, TN
hero_subtitle: Lake house, mill-era home near downtown or new build off US 321: request free roofing quotes in Lenoir City and compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers. You decide, with no obligation.
intro: Lenoir City sits immediately north of Fort Loudoun Dam, which TVA completed in 1943, and the Tennessee River forms its southern boundary. The town grew on land that was once the Lenoir family's plantation, where William Ballard Lenoir built a cotton mill in the early 1830s, and it was incorporated in 1907. Most of the city is in Loudon County, with a small part in Roane County. Interstate 75 and US 70 cross US 321 on the north side of town.

sections.heading: Mill-town streets near downtown
body: The Lenoir City Company put up its office building downtown in 1890, and that building, now home to the Lenoir City Museum, is on the National Register. The Lenoir Car Works, once the largest business in Loudon County, covered ninety-three acres along the river, and it and a knitting mill each employed several hundred workers in 1910.

Homes on the older streets near downtown can hide original board decking, multiple shingle layers and chimneys that need new flashing or repointing. Ask for a per-sheet price to replace damaged decking, so the quote covers whatever a tear-off uncovers.

sections.heading: Living on the lakes
body: Fort Loudoun Lake covers about 14,600 acres behind the dam, and a short canal links it to Tellico Lake on the Little Tennessee River. Lake lots along roads such as Lakeland Drive face open water, and wind crossing a wide stretch of lake can hit those roofs harder than it hits sheltered houses inland.

For a lakefront house, ask about the shingle's wind rating, sealed starter strips and corrosion-resistant fasteners and flashing. On a steep lot that drops toward the water, the roofer also needs a plan for getting materials down and debris out without damaging the yard, septic area or dock.

sections.heading: Newer homes along US 321
body: Much of the newer building in Lenoir City has gone up along US 321 and the Town Creek area, where the Town Creek Parkway project tied Harrison Road into the highway.

A newer roof rarely needs replacing for age, but storms and installation mistakes still cause leaks. Missing drip edge, poorly sealed pipe boots and nails placed too high are common culprits, so if a young roof is leaking, ask a roofer to check workmanship before assuming the shingles failed.

sections.heading: Between Knox and Blount counties
body: Until 2017, US 321 crossed the river on a bridge atop Fort Loudoun Dam; a new bridge just southeast of the dam now carries Lamar Alexander Parkway toward Maryville, while US 70 runs northeast to Farragut. When quotes come in, ask each roofer to break out tear-off, underlayment, roofing material, flashing, ventilation and cleanup, plus any extra charge for steep or hard-to-reach lake lots, so the numbers line up side by side.

roofing_notes: Older homes near downtown may hide board decking and several shingle layers; get a per-sheet decking price.
Lakefront roofs face open-water wind, so get the wind rating and sealed starter strips in writing.
Use corrosion-resistant fasteners and flashing on homes close to the water.
On newer homes with early leaks, have workmanship checked before assuming material failure.

faqs.q: Is Tellico Village part of Lenoir City?
faqs.a: No. Tellico Village is a separate census-designated community in Loudon County, and it has its own page on this site. Lenoir City addresses use ZIP codes 37771 and 37772. Wherever your Loudon County home is, either page will connect you with up to 3 local roofers at no cost.

faqs.q: Does Loudon County require a home improvement license for roofers?
faqs.a: Loudon County is not on the list of nine counties where Tennessee's Home Improvement license applies. A state contractor's license is still required for any job of $25,000 or more. On a smaller job, ask for proof of liability insurance, a written contract that spells out the scope, and a few local references you can actually call.

faqs.q: Can roofers get materials to a lake house that sits below the road?
faqs.a: Usually, but access affects the price and the schedule. Steep driveways and lots that fall toward the water can mean hand-carrying materials, using a conveyor or bringing a smaller dumpster. Mention the access when you request quotes, and ask each roofer how they will protect the lawn, septic area and any dock or seawall.

name: Sevierville
title: Sevierville, TN Roofing Quotes | Home & Cabin Roofers
meta_description: Free roofing quotes in Sevierville, TN, for homes, cabins and rental properties. Compare up to 3 licensed, insured Sevier County roofers, no obligation.
h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Sevierville, TN
hero_subtitle: Primary home, farm property or rental cabin in the hills, Sevierville owners can collect up to 3 free quotes from licensed, insured roofers and choose on their own schedule. No obligation.
intro: Sevierville is the county seat of Sevier County, founded in 1795 and named for John Sevier. It sits along the Little Pigeon River where the foothills of the Smokies give way to the Tennessee Valley, about ten miles north of Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Dolly Parton was born here in 1946, and her statue stands on the courthouse lawn. Roofing work in and around the city covers in-town houses, rural properties and wooded hillside cabins.

sections.heading: In town and on the outskirts
body: Sevierville's neighborhoods include Old Town, East Sevierville, South Sevierville, Riverview and Northview-Kodak, with Harrisburg and Fair Garden to the east and Catlettsburg and Boyds Creek to the north. The Sevier County Courthouse, built in the 1890s, anchors downtown. The town has rebuilt before: an 1856 fire destroyed a newly built courthouse, 41 houses and several shops. Today, Winfield Dunn Parkway (State Route 66) links the city to Interstate 40.

The Kodak area in north Sevierville, home to Smokies Stadium and a Buc-ee's, has a busy commercial side near the interstate. If your property there is a shop or office, say so on the form, since commercial work is quoted differently from a house.

sections.heading: Cabins and rental properties
body: Hillside cabins bring their own roofing problems: steep pitches, complicated rooflines around decks and dormers, tight driveways, and heavy tree cover that drops leaves and limbs.

If your cabin is a short-term rental, plan roof work around bookings. Ask each roofer how many days the job will take, whether the cabin can stay occupied, and how they will clear nails from decks, walkways and hot tub areas before guests return.

If the cabin sits up a narrow, winding road where a full-size dumpster or delivery truck cannot reach the door, raise that early. Ask how materials will get to the site, whether a smaller trailer or extra labor is already in the price, and who pays if a driveway edge or retaining wall is damaged.

sections.heading: Extremes, wildfire and material choices
body: Sevierville averages close to 49 inches of precipitation and 3.6 inches of snow a year, but its record temperatures run from 106 degrees down to 24 below zero, so roofing here has to handle real extremes.

The November 2016 wildfires, which started on the Chimney Tops Trail and were driven by high winds into Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge, are a reminder that wooded Sevier County properties face fire risk. When comparing metal and shingle options for a wooded lot, ask each roofer for the fire rating of the complete roof assembly and how gutters and valleys will be kept clear of leaf litter.

If you choose metal for a cabin, ask about snow guards above entries, decks and hot tubs. Snow is light here in most winters, but a sheet of ice sliding off a metal roof can still break a railing or hurt someone below.

roofing_notes: Schedule work on rental cabins between bookings and ask how nails and debris will be cleared from decks.
Steep, complex cabin roofs and tight driveways affect both price and schedule.
Ask for the fire rating of the full roof assembly on wooded lots.
Keep gutters and valleys clear of leaves, which hold moisture and can carry embers.

faqs.q: Can a roofer work on my cabin while guests are booked?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but it is usually easier to schedule the work between stays. Roof work is loud, and decks, walkways and hot tub areas need to be swept clear of nails before guests use them. Tell each roofer your open dates when you request quotes, and ask for a realistic start and finish window in writing.

faqs.q: Is Kodak part of Sevierville?
faqs.a: The Kodak area around Smokies Stadium is counted as part of north Sevierville, and ZIP code 37764 serves Kodak. Whether a particular address is inside city limits depends on where the property sits, so check your tax bill if it matters for a permit. Either way, you can request quotes for a Kodak home here.

faqs.q: Do Sevier County roofers need a special license?
faqs.a: Sevier County did not adopt the state Home Improvement law, so the license that applies is the state contractor's license, required for jobs of $25,000 or more. Below that amount, check insurance, written warranties and references, and be wary of anyone who knocks on doors after a storm and asks for full payment before starting.
